children.text: By immediately showing her acne without makeup or trying to hide her skin, Alix establishes herself as someone willing to be vulnerable with her audience. This is important because beauty influencers are often associated with perfect images, makeup, and carefully edited photos. Instead of beginning the TikTok by presenting an idealized version of herself, Alix shows viewers a more imperfect and realistic version. The fact that she is recording the video while sitting in her bed also contributes to this sense of authenticity. The casual bedroom setting feels personal and less staged than a professional studio, making her appear more relatable and trustworthy. These aesthetics reinforce her ethos because viewers can see her in a more natural environment while also seeing her acne for themselves. The visual and setting together suggest that social media does not always show what someone's skin actually looks like.
As Alix explains what has been happening with her skin, she uses her own personal
experience to create an emotional connection with her audience. Rather than simply giving
skincare advice, she talks about something that has affected her personally, which allows viewers
who experience acne to identify with her. This creates pathos because acne can be connected to
feelings of insecurity, embarrassment, and frustration, especially when appearance is an important
part of someone's social life. By discussing her own experience, Alix shows that even though she
is a successful beauty and lifestyle influencer, she experiences many of the same insecurities as
her audience. This helps break down the distance between influencer and viewer.

In this part of the TikTok, Alix explains her personal experience with acne and what has been happening with her skin. By sharing this context, she helps viewers understand why she is discussing the topic in the first place. Her purpose is not simply to show her acne, but to use her own experience to connect with viewers who may be dealing with similar struggles. Sharing her personal experience makes the message more relatable because she presents herself as someone who has lived through the issue rather than someone speaking about it from a distance. This also helps establish a connection between Alix and her audience, allowing viewers to see themselves in her experience. Her personal story therefore becomes an important part of her purpose: using her platform to openly discuss an issue that many of her followers may also experience.

During this section, the camera becomes part of Alix's argument because viewers can actually see the skin she is discussing. This is an example of modality because the visual presentation makes her message feel more immediate and believable. Instead of only talking about struggling with acne, Alix allows viewers to see her skin for themselves. If she only discussed her acne while showing a heavily edited or perfectly made-up version of herself, her message might feel less authentic. The video format gives her the ability to visually demonstrate what she is saying rather than relying only on words. This use of modality reinforces her relatable persona and challenges the expectation that an influencer's appearance should always be polished or perfect. The visual presentation therefore strengthens her argument by making her personal experience visible to the audience. By combining her spoken explanation with the visual evidence of her skin, Alix makes her message easier for viewers to understand and believe.
